'''Gordon:''' {{legend0|#FFB2B2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#E27F7F|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} {{legend0|#d72f30|70–80%}} {{legend0|#c21b18|80–90%}} | title = [[Governor of Wyoming|Governor]] | before_election = [[Mark Gordon]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Mark Gordon]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsWY}} The '''2022 Wyoming gubernatorial election''' took place on November 8, 2022, to elect the [[governor of Wyoming]]. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Mark Gordon]] won a second term against [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Wyoming State Facilities Commission member Theresa Livingston. Livingston's vote percentage was the lowest for a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] candidate running for governor in Wyoming since it was [[History of Wyoming|admitted to the union]] in [[1890 Wyoming gubernatorial election|1890]], falling short of Leslie Petersen's 22.90% performance in [[2010 Wyoming gubernatorial election|2010]]. Gordon won by the widest margin in the state's history, winning by 58 points and becoming the first Republican to win every county since [[2010 Wyoming gubernatorial election|2010]]. Livingston's 15.8% of the vote was the weakest performance by a major party nominee in any state since that of Republican Dan Maes in [[Colorado]] in [[2010 Colorado gubernatorial election|2010]]; however, that election featured a candidate from the [[Constitution Party (United States)|Constitution Party]] taking 36.38% of the vote.
